ds: Payment messages can be altered or structured so that names, addresses or purpose fields that would trigger sanctions screening are omitted, truncated or replaced. Controls focus on message integrity, intermediary practices and unusual patterns in message content.

rat: Payment-message manipulation in SWIFT and correspondent routing.

ind.n: Originator or beneficiary fields missing, generic or truncated
ind.cx: Payments carry placeholders such as 'customer' or incomplete addresses for parties in higher-risk jurisdictions.
ind.ds: Payment messages omit, truncate or use generic placeholder data for originator or beneficiary details.
ind.cn: Missing, incomplete or placeholder originator and beneficiary information

ind.n: Use of cover payments that omit underlying parties
ind.cx: Cover message shows only the banks, with details of ultimate parties absent.
ind.fp: Cover method is used for ordinary correspondent business.
ind.ds: Cover message shows only the banks, with details of ultimate parties absent.

ind.n: Free-text fields containing instructions to avoid mention of certain parties
ind.cx: Messages instruct downstream banks not to reference parties or contain unusual remarks.
ind.ds: Messages instruct downstream banks not to reference parties or contain unusual remarks.

ind.n: Frequent changes of intermediary banks or repeated reformatting of payments
ind.cx: Rejected payments are resubmitted with altered details.
ind.ds: Rejected payments are resubmitted with altered details.

ind.n: Payments routed through banks in jurisdictions with weak controls for no clear reason
ind.cx: Routing does not follow normal correspondent paths.
ind.ds: Routing does not follow normal correspondent paths.

ind.n: Different party name between message and underlying invoice
ind.cx: Payment shows one remitter while documents show another.
ind.ds: Payment shows one remitter while documents show another.

ind.cx: Peer institution frequently sends payments with data gaps.
ind.ds: Peer institution frequently sends payments with data gaps.

ctl.n: Payment message completeness and quality controls
ctl.ds: Rejects or queries payments with missing or meaningless party data, tracks deficiency rates and resubmissions and scorecards senders. It improves transparency of payment chains.

Sends requests for information to respondents or senders with deadlines, tracking of response quality and escalation of repeated deficiencies. It resolves unexplained activity and pressures partners to improve.

Compares the serial payment message with the accompanying cover message so that originator, beneficiary and intermediary details can be checked for consistency. It stops parties being hidden by splitting a payment chain across messages.

Screens payment instructions, references and narrative fields for restricted parties, goods, places and concealment language using tuned matching logic. It catches exposure that does not appear in the customer record.

ctl.n: Suspicion escalation and reporting decision protocol
ctl.ds: Defines timelines, owners and criteria for escalating concerns and deciding whether to report, and for documents implying payments to proscribed groups. It ensures timely, accountable decisions.

Alerts on unusual countries, corridors, deposit locations and geolocation dispersion relative to the customer profile or on activity near designated risk regions. It focuses review on geographic anomalies.

ctl.n: Periodic respondent review and volume monitoring
ctl.ds: Reviews respondent activity against expected volumes, updates expected activity and restricts routing via higher-risk banks. It keeps correspondent risk assessments current after onboarding.

Maintains records of identification, transactions, decisions and exceptions for the required period, with logs of deviations and a retrievable audit trail. It allows regulators and investigators to reconstruct events and supports later challenge of decisions.

ctl.n: Trade document review and consistency checking
ctl.ds: Trained staff and automated checks review goods, parties, routes, descriptions and codes across invoice, bill of lading and payment documents. It exposes mismatches and falsified paper.

ctl.n: Alert adjudication standards and quality assurance
ctl.ds: Defines documented criteria for clearing or escalating screening and monitoring alerts, resolves matches using secondary identifiers and samples closed alerts for quality. It makes decisions consistent, defensible and auditable.

ctl.n: Sampling, quality assurance and analytics audit
ctl.ds: Takes periodic samples of customer files, alert decisions, relied-upon files or analytical datasets and tests them for exceptions, duplicates and errors, feeding findings back to owners and training. It independently confirms that controls work as designed.

Screens customers, owners, counterparties, vessels, dealers and addresses against sanctions, enforcement and restricted-party lists at onboarding and ongoing, using fuzzy matching and secondary identifiers. Potential matches are held for adjudication before service or funds are released.

ctl.n: Scenario tuning and independent model validation
ctl.ds: Periodically tests thresholds, coverage and segmentation, including above and below the line, and independently validates scenarios and models with documented rationale for changes. It keeps detection effective and defensible.
